subtype: Approach: stretching the budget to match relatives' homes [Pitfall]
passage:
Hi Anil,

You asked how the new flat is going. Honest answer: it's lovely, and it's heavy. When Kavitha's cousin bought that big flat, we could not stop comparing, and we took the largest loan the bank would give. I was proud for about a month. Now on every payment day we count the days to the next salary. Last week the water pump broke and we had to argue about who would skip what, because there is no cushion. We have stopped putting anything aside, and even a dinner out gets a long pause. I'm not complaining about the flat itself. I just wish I had asked what we needed instead of what looked as good as theirs. Come and see us when you can.

Jomon

qa.q: What broke in the flat last week?
What does Jomon feel about the flat and the loan now?
qa.a: Jomon feels a mix of pride and regret, still fond of the flat but strained by tight money; the wish to have asked what they needed shows the regret.

qa.q: What could Jomon and Kavitha do to ease the pressure?
qa.a: They could go through their monthly costs to find what to trim and slowly rebuild a small cushion, and talk to the bank about their options, rather than measuring against others.

qa.q: How might Kavitha's cousin see the couple's situation?
qa.a: The cousin may not know about the strain and could be surprised, since the comparing happened in the couple's own minds.

grounding: Jomon and Kavitha take the maximum loan to match a cousin's larger flat and end up with no savings and stress.

subtype: Approach: stretching the budget to match relatives' homes [Pitfall]
passage:
Gopika, you asked why we never go out anymore. I'll tell you the truth. I'm Uma, and it's because of a flat.
When we started looking, my cousin Leela had just moved into a big three-bedroom in Gachibowli. At her housewarming, everyone kept saying, "When's your turn?" I felt small in our rented two-bedroom.
So Prakash and I went to the bank and asked for the maximum loan they'd give. They gave it. We bought a three-bedroom almost like Leela's.
Now nearly all our salaries go to the EMI and the maintenance. We haven't saved anything in eight months. When Prakash's father had a hospital visit last month, we had to borrow from my brother, and I lay awake all night.
The third bedroom is full of boxes. We don't even use it.
I wish I'd bought a home for us, not for that housewarming.

qa.q: Where had Uma's cousin Leela moved?
qa.a: Into a big three-bedroom in Gachibowli.

qa.q: How did Uma feel at Leela's housewarming?
qa.a: Uma felt small and embarrassed about the rented two-bedroom when everyone asked when it would be Uma's turn.

qa.q: Which approach would have suited Uma and Prakash better?
qa.a: They could have worked out a comfortable EMI from their own income first and chosen a flat within that, perhaps with a qualified adviser's help.

qa.q: How is Prakash affected by the stretched budget?
qa.a: Prakash has to cope with the father's hospital visit with no savings, so the couple has to borrow, adding worry and strain.

grounding: It shows a couple taking the maximum loan to match a cousin's larger flat, then facing tight cash flow and stress when an unexpected expense comes.

subtype: Approach: stretching the budget to match relatives' homes [Pitfall]
passage:
I've worked with Neelam at the insurance office for three years, and I watched this unfold from the next desk. I'm Irfan, by the way.
Last year her husband's elder brother moved into a large flat in Salt Lake. At lunch Neelam kept showing us photos. A few weeks later she told us they'd taken the biggest loan the bank would approve and booked a similar flat nearby.
At first she seemed thrilled. Then things changed. She stopped joining us for lunch outside and brought tiffin every day. When the office did a small collection for a colleague's farewell, she quietly said she'd skip it this month.
In November her scooter broke down, and I saw her on the phone, voice tight, asking someone if she could pay the repair in parts.
I don't know everything about their finances. But she looked tired in a way she hadn't before.

qa.q: Where did Neelam's husband's elder brother move?
qa.a: Into a large flat in Salt Lake.

qa.q: What might Neelam have been feeling on the phone about the scooter repair?
qa.a: She was probably anxious and stressed, since with the stretched loan she couldn't handle even a small unexpected cost easily.

qa.q: What else could Neelam and her husband have done when choosing a flat?
qa.a: They could have set a loan payment they could comfortably manage and chosen a flat within that, speaking to a qualified adviser if unsure.

qa.q: How do Neelam's colleagues see the change in her?
qa.a: Irfan notices she skips lunches and collections and looks tired, and seems concerned without knowing the full picture.

grounding: It shows, through a colleague's eyes, a couple taking the maximum loan to match a relative's larger flat, then facing tight cash flow and stress over unexpected costs.
